text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- Russia and Chechnya accuse each other of terrorism. These accusations may threaten peace talks between Moscow and Grozny.
- The Deputy director of the Federal Bankruptcy Administration Pyotr Karpov was arrested for alleged bribe taking. It may be one more effort to boost the anti-corruption campaign.
- Former Chechen Finance Minister and chairman of the board of a Moscow bank Alik Suleimenov is detained in Moscow for an alleged attempt to embezzle 13 billion roubles.
- A lot of oil is turning into a lot of problems for Azerbaijan -- the route of the main export pipeline is not yet decided.
- Russia's Central Bank said the system of payments would be reformed within two or three years.
- The precious metals market in Russia is to be liberalised.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The recent terrorist acts in southern Russia proved that Chechen president Aslan Maskhadov cannot control the republic, and Moscow cannot control the surrounding regions.
- A prominent Moscow lawyer does not rule out political motives behind the arrest of Pyotr Karpov, formerly a close aide to First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov is trying to bring the production-sharing law into force.
- The system of running of state controlled enterprises will be changed, says Viktor Pylnev, deputy chairman of the Sate property Committee.
- The Central Bank is changing regulations for banks with foreign capital. NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia's political authorities and security services have proved their total inability to protect the country's citizens from terrorism.

- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais is right behind President Yeltsin in the list of 100 Russia's leading polititians published by the paper. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin occupies the third place.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The State Duma lower house of the parliament has prepared a bill on incorporating new members into the Russian Federation. This bill may be used in debates on possible unification with Belarus.
PRAVDA-5

- World Bank money which has disappeared in Russia is unaccounted for. But when the time comes to pay the loans back, the World Bank will recommend that the authorities rob their own people, the opposition paper says.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- The president is determined to lead Russia out of crisis, says Boris Nemtsov.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
